result.summary:
FAIL. Design doc lib/letflow/design/iss0768-role-registry-tenant-prefix.md contains real implementation code -- multiple fenced Elixir code blocks giving exact, copy-pasteable call-site rewrites, not just signatures/prose. This directly violates the CODE-DESIGNER mandate ('no function bodies, no actual .ex/.exs code blocks') and acceptance criterion 'No .ex function body / implementation code present anywhere in the design doc'. Per WF-02 Step 1b, one failed check fails the whole gate -- no partial credit -- so this alone is sufficient for FAIL regardless of the doc's other strengths.

Evidence of the violation (fenced code blocks at lines 33-36, 48-50, 56-63, 73-80, 105-112, 118-125, 141-143, 148-150, 159-161, 165-167 of the design doc -- 10 blocks total, confirmed via `grep -n '^```'`):
- Lines 48-50: literal rewritten call `Repo.all(from(t in TenantRole, order_by: [asc: t.name]), prefix: opts[:prefix])` -- an exact, pasteable expression, not a signature.
- Lines 118-125: literal rewritten `Repo.insert(conflict_target: :name, on_conflict: [set: [group_id: group_id]], returning: true, prefix: opts[:prefix])` call.
- Lines 141-143, 148-150, 159-161, 165-167: literal router body rewrites, e.g. `handle_list_roles(conn, conn.assigns.scoped_opts)` and `defp handle_list_roles(conn, opts)` given as exact code to drop into the route macro bodies.
These go beyond '@spec + def name/arity' (which IS permitted per the CODE-DESIGNER role and appears correctly at lines 33-36, 56-63, 73-80, 105-112 as signature blocks) into showing ELIXIR-DEV the literal implementation, which is exactly the failure mode this gate exists to catch (design step skipped in substance even though the artefact exists).

Positive findings, for the record (would have been PASS on these dimensions alone):
- ISS-0768's affected_files and Repo-call inventory (Repo.all, Repo.get_by, Repo.get, Repo.transaction, Repo.insert) are all accounted for. Verified by direct read of lib/letflow/identity/role_registry.ex: Repo.all (line 41, list_roles), Repo.get_by (line 75, resolve_role_in_tx), Repo.transaction (line 84) + Repo.get (line 85, both inside do_upsert_role), Repo.insert (line 98, insert_or_update_role) -- exactly 5 calls, matching the issue's own grep-derived inventory. Design §1.1-1.4 covers all 4 in-scope calls; §3 explicitly addresses the 5th (resolve_role_in_tx's Repo.get_by) as reasoned out-of-scope rather than silently skipped.
- Router call-site claims verified against the actual current lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex, not the design doc's paraphrase: lines 203-209 (`handle_list_roles(conn)` / `handle_upsert_role(conn)` inside authz_get/authz_post "/roles") and lines 650-677 (handle_list_roles/1 body calling `RoleRegistry.list_roles()` at line 651; handle_upsert_role/1 body calling `RoleRegistry.upsert_role(name, group_id)` at line 669) match the design doc's cited line numbers and current signatures exactly. The design's cited example at line 143 (`handle_create(conn, conn.assigns.scoped_opts)`) also matches the real file verbatim.
- resolve_role_in_tx/1's 'zero current callers' claim checked via `grep -rn resolve_role_in_tx --include=*.ex --include=*.exs .` (excluding role_registry.ex itself): the only hits are in test/letflow/role_registry_test.exs (direct unit-test calls). No production module (router, Identity, Engine) calls it. Claim holds.
- §4's regression-investigation section gives three concrete, directly-runnable git commands (`git log -p --follow`, `git log -p --follow -S"prefix"`, `git log --follow --diff-filter=A --format=%H`) with stated decision criteria for each outcome -- mechanically runnable, not vague guidance.

Required rework for CODE-DESIGNER: strip every fenced code block that shows a call-site rewrite as literal executable syntax (§1.1's Repo.all snippet, §1.4's Repo.insert snippet, all of §2's route-macro/handler-body snippets) and replace with prose description of the change (which argument gains which option, in which position) plus the @spec/def name+arity only, matching the style already correctly used for the function-signature blocks.
